speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. How many weeks pregnant are you, and have you experienced any abdominal pain or vaginal bleeding?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old female at 30 weeks gestation. The patient presents with a sudden onset of fever, headache, anorexia, fatigue, and malaise. She reports the consumption of ice cream 3 days prior to the onset of symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any sensitivity to light or neck stiffness, and have you noticed any changes in your vision or swelling in your hands and face? I also need to know if you have experienced any abdominal pain or contractions.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Fever. I also have Headache, Anorexia, Fatigue, Malaise.

speaker: Doctor
text: Have you consumed any unpasteurized dairy products or soft cheeses recently, and are you experiencing any abdominal pain or vaginal bleeding? I would also like to check your blood pressure and perform a physical exam for any signs of infection.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Unremarkable. The patient is currently pregnant, at her 30th week of gestation. Social history: Non-smoker, does not consume alcohol. No recent travels or contact with sick individuals. No known allergies.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your recent consumption of ice cream and current symptoms, I suspect a listerial infection. REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture, Urine_Culture, CBC.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood Cultures: Gram-positive rods that are catalase-positive and show distinctive tumbling motility in the liquid medium. Complete Blood Count: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, Platelets 200,000 /μL. Urinalysis: Appearance Clear, WBC 0-5 /HPF, RBC 0-2 /HPF, Protein Negative, Glucose Negative. (Note: Urine Culture results were not provided in the available data, but Urinalysis shows normal readings).

speaker: Doctor
text: The blood culture results confirming Gram-positive rods with tumbling motility are diagnostic for Listeria monocytogenes. DIAGNOSIS READY: Listeriosis
